title: When a reply fails — the new error card

steps.path: A reply that failed because Anthropic was busy
steps.headline: A busy provider now says so in plain words and offers Try again, which re-runs the reply without a new message.
steps.changed: "Overloaded (provider error 529)" becomes "Anthropic is overloaded right now. The app tried again for about a minute." The provider's words fold under Details; Switch model and Try again sit below.
steps.notice: One press carries on. Nothing new appears in the conversation, and anything the assistant already did stays done.
steps.risk: Try again runs the reply again, so it costs another request if the provider is still busy.

steps.path: A reply that failed on Anthropic's monthly spending cap
steps.headline: An account problem names the fix: Open billing goes to Anthropic's billing page, and Switch model lets you carry on now.
steps.changed: The raw sentence becomes "Anthropic stopped this reply: your spending limit has been reached." There is no Try again, because it could only fail the same way.
steps.notice: Open billing goes straight to the place that fixes it, instead of leaving you to find it.
steps.risk: Open billing opens Anthropic's site in your browser; if you are signed out there you sign in first.

steps.path: A reply that failed because the Anthropic key was rejected
steps.headline: A rejected key says so and offers Open settings, the screen where the key is changed.
steps.changed: "invalid x-api-key (provider error 401)" becomes "Anthropic didn't accept your API key." with Open settings.
steps.notice: One press to the key, the same as OpenRouter's rejected-key card already does.

steps.path: A reply that failed because the conversation outgrew the model
steps.headline: A conversation too long for the model offers Summarise and continue.
steps.changed: "prompt is too long: 1048213 tokens > 1000000 maximum" becomes "This conversation is too long for this model." Summarise and continue condenses older messages, then tries the reply again.
steps.notice: The conversation recovers in one press instead of looking broken.
steps.risk: Summarising loses detail from older messages (the summary itself stays visible in the chat).

steps.path: A reply that failed for a reason the app does not recognise
steps.headline: An error the app can't explain keeps the provider's exact words and now offers Report bug and Try again.
steps.changed: The words are unchanged — the app never guesses a cause it doesn't know. Report bug opens the bug report with the error attached; Try again re-runs the reply.
steps.notice: There is always a way forward, even for an error nobody has seen before.
steps.risk: The sentence can be long and technical, as today.

steps.path: The end of a reply that ran out of steps
steps.headline: A reply that hit its step limit says so plainly and offers Keep going.
steps.changed: "Response ended: max_steps." becomes "Stopped after reaching the step limit for one reply." A line under it — "The task isn't finished." — carries Keep going, which continues the same task.
steps.notice: No message to type to carry on; the button only appears under the newest reply.
steps.risk: Easy to keep pressing on a task that is going in circles — the step limit in Settings still applies to each round.
